group:paper-mock-nb-2026-m2:seven-choice.overview: 作者回顾与滑板相伴的一生：11岁用破旧滑板体会到骑行的自由，少年时和伙伴一起滑，大学时四处找地方滑，后来以滑板写作出版为业，如今又把这份热爱传给了孩子。
group:paper-mock-nb-2026-m2:seven-choice.fullTranslationZh:
我与滑板的缘分始于1975年，我一下子就迷上了它。11岁生日时，父亲给我买了第一块滑板。它装着廉价的陶土轮子，滑起来又晃又颠，还响个不停。然而，当我感受到滑行带来的自由时，这些都不重要了。这段早年的经历让我明白：热爱不在于拥有最好的装备，而在于它带给你的感觉。

很快，我就每期必读《滑板人》——当时一本很受欢迎的杂志，而我们街区到处都是一起玩滑板的孩子。我们自己搭滑道，一连几个小时沿着各家门前的车道往下滑。那种共享的自由感改变了我，对一个在传统团体运动中从不出众的人来说尤其如此。

1983年，滑板陪我去了多伦多上大学。有一次，一位在城北约克大学读书的朋友提议我们去试试大学里的隧道。然而我们发现隧道关闭了，这反倒促使我去探索别的地方——空旷的停车场、安静的办公园区和平整的小路。从这些经历中得到的快乐从未离开过我。

随着年龄增长，我与滑板的关系也成熟起来。我创建了一个名为SkateGeezer的网站，专门面向在20世纪60、70和80年代玩过滑板的人。它启发我写了一本书——《混凝土浪潮》。从那以后，我最终在滑板杂志社开始了出版方面的职业生涯。

如今，我有了自己的家庭，那份热爱仍在延续。孩子们几乎刚会走路，我就带他们接触滑板。看到儿子们超越我自己的水平，这种圆满的时刻带来的自豪无可比拟。我知道，有些旅程只要你坚持下去，就不会结束。它们只是找到了新的、美好的前进道路。

completedSourceTexts.text: My journey with skateboarding began in 1975, and I was immediately hooked(钩住). For my 11th birthday, my father bought me my first board. It had cheap clay wheels that shook, bumped and made much noise. Yet, none of that mattered when I felt the freedom of the ride. This early experience taught me that passion isn’t about having the best equipment, but about the feeling it gives you.

Soon enough, I found myself reading every issue of Skateboarder, a popular magazine back then, and our neighborhood was full of kids skating together. We built skating tracks and spent hours riding down driveways. The sense of shared freedom was transformative, especially for someone who never stood out at traditional team sports.

In 1983, my skateboard accompanied me to university in Toronto. At one point, a friend who was a student at York, north of the city, suggested we try the tunnels at the university. Yet, we found them closed, which only pushed me to explore other places – empty parking lots, quiet office parks, and smooth pathways. The joy I got from these experiences never left me.

As I grew older, my relationship with skateboarding matured. I created a website called SkateGeezer dedicated to skaters who had ridden in the 1960s, 70s and 80s. It inspired me to write a book, The Concrete Wave. From there, I eventually built a career in publishing at skateboarding magazines.

Now, with a family of my own, that passion rides on. I introduced all my children to skateboarding almost as soon as they could walk. The full-circle moment of seeing my sons surpass my own ability is a pride unlike any other. I know some journeys, when you stick with them, don’t end. They just find new, beautiful paths forward.
